summary: Preserved PR 985's working memory-budget activation and replaced its query-only chunk loop with request-local Q/K grouping. This keeps the global PAGED table aligned with global request row IDs and bounds each logits allocation by a request-local K width.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact-candidate failing-before evidence: 2 failed. RAGGED allocated 48 bytes against a 24-byte budget; PAGED later passed a sliced table with global row IDs. Raw output: candidate-counterexamples-before.log
2 passed after correction: request-local allocations stayed within budget and RAGGED/PAGED metadata mappings were preserved. Raw output: counterexamples-after.log
11 passed across candidate regressions, independent counterexamples, and the existing non-kpool budget suite. Raw output: regression-after.log

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015. Tests allocated real fp8 and metadata tensors on device and exercised production orchestration; DeepGEMM/top-k were mocked.
remaining_limitations: No GLM-5.3-Flash or RadixArk weights were available.
The reported four-B300 CUDA TP=4/EP=4 serving workload, long-context traffic, hierarchical cache, and DFLASH execution were not reproduced on the single AMD GPU.
NVIDIA DeepGEMM allocation behavior, the actual fused top-k kernel, and end-to-end semantic accuracy remain unverified locally.

A single request whose own pooled K width exceeds the memory budget cannot be split further by this scheme; the reviewed counterexample concerned the avoidable concatenated multi-request K width, which is now removed.
